land.text: Tsang and Ü, the Tsangpa realm with Shigatse: 'The Tsangpa stronghold, Shigatse, was captured after a long and bloody siege in March 1642'

predecessors.note: Taken 1641-1642. Kham came from the king of Beri (Donyo Dorje) in 1641 and Qinghai from the Mongol prince Choghtu Khong Tayiji in 1637. Cliopatria's Tibet row (1363-1952) covers Ü-Tsang, Kham and half of Qinghai throughout; the ea-06 Tibet owner must decide whether it is the Ganden Phodrang under Khoshut protection (a vassal tint) or the same land.

land.text: Lhasa and Central Tibet, left to the Tibetan government (Ganden Phodrang) when the Khoshut khan died in December 1717; the Dzungars held it under occupation from 1717 to 1720

successors.note: The Khoshut Khanate page lists 'Dzungar Khanate' as successor, and the Dzungar conquest page says 'The conquest also ended the Khoshut Khanate, as their Khan had died'. The same page describes the Dzungars' stay as 'the occupation of the region lasting from 1717 to 1720' under 'a military government', never an annexation, so the land is Tibet's and the Dzungars are its occupiers (fx-54, 3 Nov 2026). The Qing annexation of Qinghai and eastern Kham is undated on that page; the Qing expelled the Dzungars from Tibet in 1720 and made Amdo the province of Qinghai in 1724.

land.text: Amdo, made the province of Qinghai in 1724

successors.note: fx-48 (3 Nov 2026): Tibet under Qing rule: 'The Qing made the region of Amdo into the province of Qinghai in 1724'. The Khoshuts of Tibet end in December 1717 (infobox 'Disestablished: 1717'); this dossier carries only the Kokonor (Qinghai) Khoshuts of Güshi's line on to 1724, so that Qinghai is not nobody's for six years. The pages are silent on their rule in 1718-1722: confidence 1.

capitals.name: Dam (Damxung, by Nam Tso)
capitals.note: Weak: the Güshi Khan page says only that Güshi 'spent summers at Dam by Tengri-nor' (no year); the Khoshut page names no capital. Shigatse (the Dalai Lama led to its palace in 1642) and Lhasa are the cities of the pages.

capitals.name: Lhasa
capitals.note: 'In 1705-6, Lhazang entered Lhasa, put the regent to death, and deposed the 6th Dalai Lama'; the Potala Palace was attacked in December 1717 and Lhazang died (Dzungar conquest of Tibet page).

correction.text: empty: no Khoshut state existed before 1637; the Hexi-Hami cells are not Khoshut

keyframe_review.note: 291,359 km2 for 1582-99 (90.2-101.1 E, 38.4-43.5 N: the Hexi-Hami belt, Gansu 522 cells, Hami-Turfan 328, Xinjiang 471): no page opened puts the Khoshuts here. The Khoshut page has the Oirats from Tuva, under the Northern Yuan khans until Esen's death in 1455, with no state before 1636; the Güshi Khan page has the Khoshut chiefs fighting near the Ishim and Tobol rivers in 1630. Cliopatria's row starts in 1582 by taking 1,104 cells from its Tümed shape (the Tumed dossier marks that loss nobody). The Khoshut Khanate page gives no infobox area. Draw nothing as Khoshut.

291,359 km2 for 1609-35: as for 1582. The Dzungar-Qing Wars and Khoshut pages date the Khoshut rise to 1636-1642; in 1625 and 1630 the Khoshut chiefs were fighting each other (Güshi Khan page: Chöükür and Baibaghas).

correction.text: Qinghai (Kokonor): Güshi's 1637 victory near Qinghai Lake, 'the Battle of the Bloody Hill' on the Kokonor Gorge

keyframe_review.note: 291,481 km2 for 1636-44: Cliopatria's Hexi-Hami shape again. The Khoshuts are in Qinghai, not here: 'In the company of the Dzungar prince Erdeni Batur, Güshi marched into Qinghai with 10,000 Oirat troops in 1636', defeated Choghtu in 1637 'near Qinghai Lake', subdued Kham by 1641 and took Shigatse in 1642 (Khoshut page: 'Established: 1642', 'On 13 April 1642, the 5th Dalai Lama proclaimed Güshi the khan of Tibet'). The correction is the 1637 core, Qinghai; the ledger gains of 1641 (Kham) and 1642 (Central Tibet) add the rest.

correction.text: Ü-Tsang, Kham and the Kokonor (Qinghai) country under the Khoshut khan of Tibet

keyframe_review.note: 291,381 km2 for 1645-52: Hexi-Hami again. The Khoshut Khanate of 1642 held Tibet: 'With the taking of Shigatse in 1642, Güshi had brought all of Tibet under the control of the Gelug school'; Güshi 'accepted the nominal suzerainty of the Qing dynasty in 1654'. The correction is Ü-Tsang, Kham and Qinghai (8,354 cells).

correction.text: Ü-Tsang, Kham and the Kokonor (Qinghai) country under the Khoshut khan of Tibet

keyframe_review.note: 291,729 km2 for 1653-82: as for 1645. Güshi died in January 1655 and 'Tenzin Dorje, Dayan Khan, succeeded him as khan of Tibet'; 'Tenzin Dalai Khan: 1668-1696 (son)'; eight of his sons settled the Tsongön Lake region in Amdo after 1648 (Güshi Khan page).

The Khoshut khanate still held Tibet and Qinghai (Dalai Khan 1668-1696).

Ü-Tsang, Kham and the Kokonor (Qinghai) country under the Khoshut khan of Tibet

keyframe_review.note: 166,169 km2 for 1691-95: as for 1683; Cliopatria gives all 647 cells to its Qing shape in 1696 (no page of this dossier dates that), and it has no row for the Khoshut after 1695, though the khanate lasted to 1717.

correction.text: Ü-Tsang, Kham and the Kokonor (Qinghai) country under Lhazang Khan

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Khoshut shape for 1696-1717 although the khanate ended in December 1717 (Khoshut page: 'Disestablished: 1717'; 'Lhazang became khan in 1703'; 'In 1705-6, Lhazang entered Lhasa'). Ü-Tsang, Kham and Qinghai as in 1642-95. The Khoshut Khanate page gives no area. The Khoshut of Qinghai after 1717 and the 1723-24 rising are outside the pages opened (the Dzungar-Qing Wars page has 'a Dzungar uprising in Qinghai' in 1723 and does not mention Lobzang Danjin).

correction.text: the Kokonor (Qinghai) country of Güshi's line, 1718-1724

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (fx-48, 3 Nov 2026): Ü-Tsang goes to the Dzungars in December 1717 and Kham is released, so only Qinghai remains. Tibet under Qing rule: 'Lobsang Danjin, a grandson of Güshi Khan, led a rebellion in 1723' and 'The Qing made the region of Amdo into the province of Qinghai in 1724'. No page opened describes the Kokonor Khoshuts in 1718-1722 (confidence 1). Cliopatria has no Khoshut shape after 1695.

region.text: Qinghai (Kokonor): the country round Qinghai Lake

ledger.note: 1637: Güshi Khan defeats Choghtu near Qinghai Lake and holds the Kokonor country. 'In the company of the Dzungar prince Erdeni Batur, Güshi marched into Qinghai with 10,000 Oirat troops in 1636'; 'A battle took place in 1637, on the Kokonor Gorge and is known as the Battle of the Bloody Hill'; lead: 'In 1637, Güshi Khan defeated a rival Mongol prince Choghtu Khong Tayiji, a Kagyu follower, near Qinghai Lake'. The infobox of the Khoshut Khanate page has 'Established: 1642' (the khan of Tibet proclaimed in April 1642); 1637 is the first year the Khoshuts hold land. The page names the lake, not an outline: Qinghai is my reading.

region.text: Kham, the realm of the king of Beri, Donyo Dorje

ledger.note: 1639: Güshi moves against Beri. 'The campaign was prepared in 1639, assisted by some Tibetans.' 'In June of that year, Güshi moved against Beri and subjugated most of Donyo Dorje's subjects.'

1641: the king of Beri is crushed. 'In the winter of 1640-1641, Güshi crushed the king of Beri, Donyo Dorje, and then the ruler of Tsangpa'; the Güshi Khan page: 'Having subdued Kham entirely by 1641'.

1641: Kham passes to the Khoshuts. 'Having subdued Kham entirely by 1641, Güshi proceeded to invade the domain of Karma Tenkyong in Tsang' (Güshi Khan page); Khoshut page: 'In the winter of 1640-1641, Güshi crushed the king of Beri, Donyo Dorje'. Kham is the page's word.

region.text: the domain of Karma Tenkyong in Tsang

ledger.note: 1641: Güshi invades Tsang. 'Having subdued Kham entirely by 1641, Güshi proceeded to invade the domain of Karma Tenkyong in Tsang.' The Tsangpa page: 'In 1641, the leader of the Khoshut Mongols of the Kokonor region' ...

March 1642: Shigatse falls. 'The Tsangpa stronghold, Shigatse, was captured after a long and bloody siege in March 1642.' The Güshi Khan page: the castle surrendered on the 25th day of the 2nd month (25 March).

region.text: Tsang and Ü, the Tsangpa realm

ledger.note: 1642: the Tsangpa realm passes to Güshi. The Tsangpa page: the dynasty 'dominated large parts of Tibet from 1565 to 1642' (infobox 'Disestablished: 1642'; 'Karma Tenkyong (last)'); the Khoshut page: 'With the taking of Shigatse in 1642, Güshi had brought all of Tibet under the control of the Gelug school'. The Tsangpa realm is Tsang and Ü, with the West Tibetan states it had conquered in 1612-1619; Central Tibet is my reading.

13 April 1642: the 5th Dalai Lama proclaims Güshi khan of Tibet and the Khoshut Khanate is established. 'On 13 April 1642, the 5th Dalai Lama proclaimed Güshi the khan of Tibet.' Infobox: 'Established: 1642'. The Güshi Khan page: 'Güshi Khan then declared that he bestowed the supreme authority of Tibet on Dalai Lama'; the government was the Gelug-led Ganden Phodrang 'set up ... in 1642'.

August 1717: the Dzungars enter Tibet. 'On August 25th of 1717, the Dzungars passed through the Largin pass' and the page speaks of fighting 'in the Summer of 1717, after the Dzungar arrival on Tibet'; 'The Dzungar army soon reached the city of Lhasa by October 8th of 1717' (the page's infobox dates the conquest 1716-1720). Reviewer (2026-10-19): month changed from 10 to 8 on the same page; the zone is the approach to Lhasa through northern Central Tibet.
December 1717: Lhazang Khan dies at the Potala. 'Potala Palace was attacked, subsequently leading to the death of Lha-bzang Khan'; 'on November 30th of 1717, Lhasa was attacked by Tseren Dhondup'.

region.text: Lhasa and Central Tibet, left to the Tibetan government when the Khoshut khan dies

ledger.note: December 1717: Khoshut rule in Central Tibet ends. 'Later on December 2nd of 1717, Potala Palace was attacked, subsequently leading to the death of Lha-bzang Khan'; 'The conquest also ended the Khoshut Khanate, as their Khan had died and their rule had perished from the capture of Lhasa.' The Dzungars then held Lhasa under 'a military government' for 'the occupation of the region lasting from 1717 to 1720' but the page never annexes it, so the land goes to the Tibetan government (tibet), which the Khoshuts had protected since 1642; the Dzungar occupation is hatched over it (dzungar-khanate ledger/15, tibet ledger/19). Mirror of the tibet gain of December 1717. fx-54 (3 Nov 2026): was a loss to dzungar-khanate, matched by a Dzungar gain.

region.text: Kham, which the Khoshuts no longer hold

ledger.note: December 1717: Kham leaves the Khoshuts with the khanate of Tibet. fx-48 (3 Nov 2026): the dissolve used to release Kham with everything else in December 1717; with the dissolve moved to 1724 for Qinghai this loss keeps that behaviour. The Dzungar conquest page says only that the collapse 'led to the Qing annexation of modern day Qinghai and eastern Kham' (undated), so who held Kham in 1718-1725 is left to the Tibet dossier (counterpart nobody).

region.text: Amdo and the Kokonor country, made the province of Qinghai in 1724

ledger.note: 1723: Lobsang Danjin's rebellion in Qinghai. Tibet under Qing rule: 'Lobsang Danjin, a grandson of Güshi Khan, led a rebellion in 1723, when 200,000 Tibetans and Mongols attacked Xining.' The page puts the suppression 'in less than a year' without a date; the Dzungar-Qing Wars page (opened in the first pass) has 'a Dzungar uprising in Qinghai' in 1723. A grandson of Güshi leading the Kokonor princes is the page's evidence that the Khoshut line still held Qinghai in 1723.

region.text: Amdo and the Kokonor country, made the province of Qinghai in 1724

ledger.note: 1724: the rebellion is over and Qinghai is a province. 'The Qing made the region of Amdo into the province of Qinghai in 1724' (the page dates the suppression only as less than a year after the 1723 rising).

region.text: Amdo and the Kokonor country, made the province of Qinghai in 1724

ledger.note: 1724: Qinghai passes to the Qing. 'The Qing made the region of Amdo into the province of Qinghai in 1724.' Mirror of qing-dynasty ledger/36 (gain from khoshut-khanate, 1724). BRIDGE (fx-48, 3 Nov 2026): the Khoshut Khanate page has 'Disestablished: 1717' and no page opened describes the Kokonor Khoshuts in 1718-1722, so Qinghai is carried as Khoshut land from December 1717 to 1724 on the strength of the 1723 rising of Güshi's grandson; confidence 1 for those years.

region.text: Amdo and the Kokonor country, made the province of Qinghai in 1724

ledger.note: 1724: the Khoshuts of Qinghai end when the Qing make Amdo the province of Qinghai ('The Qing made the region of Amdo into the province of Qinghai in 1724'). fx-48 (3 Nov 2026): this was dated December 1717 and took Ü-Tsang, Kham and Qinghai together ('the collapse of the Khoshut Khanate', Dzungar conquest of Tibet page; infobox 'Disestablished: 1717', 'Successor: Dzungar Khanate'); Ü-Tsang now goes to the Dzungars by the loss of December 1717 and Kham by the loss above, so only Qinghai stays to 1724, six years in which the first compile left it to nobody before qing-dynasty/ledger/36 gained it. The same pages give nothing on the Khoshuts of Qinghai between 1718 and 1722.

wars.name: Güshi Khan's invasion of Qinghai

zones.text: Qinghai (Kokonor): the Battle of the Bloody Hill on the Kokonor Gorge, near Qinghai Lake

wars.outcome: Khoshut victory in 1637 over Choghtu Khong Tayiji, whom the Khoshut page has led a 30,000 strong army and the Güshi page calls a Khalkha leader.
wars.note: The Dzungar Khanate page has the same expedition: 'In 1636, Güshi led 10,000 Oirats in an invasion of Qinghai'. Reviewer (2026-10-19): 'from' set to 1637, the start of this state; Güshi 'marched into Qinghai with 10,000 Oirat troops in 1636' (Güshi Khan page), before the khanate held land.

wars.name: Güshi Khan's conquest of Kham and Tsang
wars.outcome: The king of Beri was crushed in 1640-41, Kham subdued by 1641 and Shigatse taken in March 1642; the Dalai Lama proclaimed Güshi khan of Tibet on 13 April 1642.

wars.name: Khoshut expedition to Bhutan
wars.outcome: 'Güshi Khan and the regent sent several hundred Mongol and Tibetan troops into Bhutan in 1644'; no result or land is named.

wars.name: Dzungar conquest of Tibet
wars.outcome: Dzungar victory: Tseren Dhondup took Lhasa on 30 November 1717 and Lhazang Khan died in December; the Khoshut Khanate collapsed.
wars.note: The infobox dates the war 1716-1720 (the Qing expedition of 1720 expelled the Dzungars).

certainty.note: The Khoshut lands are a mountain and plateau realm whose frontiers no page opened describes; Qinghai, Kham and Tibet are named regions, not lines. Nominal suzerainty of the Qing from 1654 (Khoshut page) fixed no border.
Only the 1723 rising and the 1724 province are dated; the Kokonor Khoshut line in 1718-1722 is a bridge between the fall of Lhasa and the Qing province.

notes:
Cliopatria's Khoshut Khanate (1582-1695) is not the Khoshut state: the nine shapes lie in the Hexi-Hami belt (90-101 E, 38-43 N), where no page puts the Khoshuts, and the row stops in 1695 while the khanate ran to 1717. The pages: the Khoshuts march into Qinghai in 1636, beat Choghtu in 1637, take Kham by 1641, Shigatse in March 1642, are proclaimed khans of Tibet on 13 April 1642 and fall to the Dzungars in December 1717. All nine Cliopatria shapes are therefore wrong; the first three (1582-1635) are corrected to empty (draw nothing) and the next five to the real Khoshut land, with one new keyframe for 1696-1717. Start: 1637 (the first land held) against the infobox's 1642 (the khan of Tibet); a rename event in April 1642 records the proclamation. Overlap: Cliopatria's Tibet row (tibet, ea-06) covers Ü-Tsang, Kham and half of Qinghai in 1642-1717 (about 6,000 cells); the ea-06 owner must decide whether Tibet is the same land, a client of the Khoshuts (the Güshi Khan page has Güshi bestowing 'the supreme authority of Tibet' on the Dalai Lama; the Khoshut page has Güshi accepting 'the nominal suzerainty of the Qing dynasty in 1654') or the Ganden Phodrang. Here the Khoshut khanate holds the land directly, as the Khoshut page treats it. Counterparts needing a dossier: tsangpa-dynasty (Tsangpa page: 1565-1642, capital Shigatse; Cliopatria has no row, its land is inside the Tibet row), Beri (Donyo Dorje's kingdom in Kham, minor), Choghtu Khong Tayiji's Kokonor Mongols (a Khalkha leader on the Güshi page, but Cliopatria's Tümed row sits on Qinghai), and the Qing (ea-08) for the 1654 nominal suzerainty (a vassal_start with counterpart khoshut-khanate) and for the 1720 and 1723-24 steps. The dzungar-khanate dossier should carry the December 1717 gain of Central Tibet and the 1720 loss. Unsettled: the Khoshuts of Qinghai from 1717 to the 1723-24 rising (the Lobzang Danjin pages Lobzang_Danjin and Lobzang_Tenzin did not load; the Dzungar-Qing War page title did not load, Dzungar-Qing_Wars did); the Khoshut capital (Dam, by the Güshi page, summers only); the ruler list (Güshi 1642-1655, Dayan Khan, Tenzin Dalai Khan 1668-1696, Lhazang 1703-1717 are on the pages but the middle reigns are not dated, so no rulers strip); the Khoshut homeland before 1636 (Ishim and Tobol rivers in 1630, Dzungaria with Erdeni Batur in 1636). The Khoshut Khanate page gives no infobox area and no capital. Gazetteer: Central Tibet, Kham and Qinghai (region) exist; 'Damxung' is not a gazetteer place (only coordinates used).

fx-48 (3 Nov 2026): the state now runs to 1724 as the Kokonor (Qinghai) Khoshuts after December 1717 (loss of Central Tibet to the Dzungars and of Kham; keyframe khoshut-khanate_1718; 1723 contest and 1724 loss to the Qing). The Khoshut Khanate page's 'Disestablished: 1717' is the khanate of Tibet; the Kokonor line is a bridge so that Qinghai is not nobody's land in 1718-1723 (window p1720-p1729's request R087). Page opened: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibet_under_Qing_rule (Lobsang_Danjin did not load; the Khoshut Khanate page has nothing on Qinghai after 1717). fx-54 (3 Nov 2026): ledger/10 is now a loss of Central Tibet to tibet (the Khoshut Khanate ended with the khan's death; the Dzungars only occupied), and identity.successors[0] is tibet; the Dzungar dossier carries the occupation.
